tldr: Headlines across 12 outlet clusters frame the Flores earthquake almost entirely through its escalating death toll and the gap between survivor needs and aid delivery; Indonesian state media projects government competence while the Malay Mail’s ‘We’re on our own’ captures abandonment, and Vatican News alone registers Catholic-community disruption on Flores.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline to carry direct survivor voice — ‘We’re on our own’ — as a front-matter quote, contrasting sharply with Indonesian state media’s aid-mobilisation framing and making abandonment the lead claim rather than a secondary detail.

Only headline to name the cancellation of a Catholic festival, foregrounding religious-community identity on Flores; the second Vatican News headline uniquely surfaces children’s education disruption, citing Save the Children — both angles absent from all secular coverage.
Only outlet to lead with the aftershock count (‘Nearly 1,600 aftershocks’) as the defining metric of ongoing seismic danger, rather than the primary death toll that anchors every other headline.

Earliest item in the cluster: headline reports only five deaths and foregrounds tsunami waves; the tsunami angle disappears entirely from subsequent coverage as the warning was lifted, making this headline uniquely time-stamped to the first hour.

bottom_line: The headline layer of Flores earthquake coverage is dominated by escalating casualty counts and unmet aid needs, with Indonesian state media projecting government competence while the Malay Mail’s survivor-voice headline signals abandonment — Vatican News alone registers the Catholic-community dimension constitutive of Flores’s identity.
